div.head: Af El. 11
div.ab: Þis sint ða domas þe ðu him settan scealt: Gif hwa gebycgge cristenne þeow, VI gear ðeowige he; ðy siofoðan beo he frioh órceapunga; mid swelce hrægle he ineode, mid swelce gange he út. Gif he wíf self hæbbe, gange hio út mid him. Gif se hlaford him þonne wif sealde, sie hio ⁊ hire bearn þæs hlafordes. Gif se þeowa þonne cweðe: ‘Nelle ic from minum hlaforde ne from minum wife ne from minum bearne ne from minum ierfe’, brenge hine þonne his hlaford to ðære dura þæs temples ⁊ þurhþyrlige his eare mid æle, to tácne þæt he sie æfre siððan þeow.

Þis sindon þa domas þe ðu him settan scealt: Gif hwa gebicge cristenne þeow, VI gear ðeowige he; ði seofoðan beo he freoh órceapunge. Mid swilce hrægle he ineode, mid swilce ga he út. Gif he wif habbe sylf, gange heo út mid him. Gif se hlaford him ðonne wif sealde, si héo ⁊ hyre bearn ðas hlafordes. Gif se ðeowa ðonne cweðe: ‘nelle ic fram minum hlaforde ne fram minum wife ne fram minum bearne ne fram minum yrfe’, brynge hine ðonne his hlaford æt ðas temples dura ⁊ ðurhðirlige his eare mid ále, to tacne þæt he sie æfre syððan þeow.

Ðis synt þa domas ðe þu heom settan scealt: Gif hwa gebycge cristene þeow, syx gear þeowie he; ⁊ on þam seofoþan beo he freo on ceapunge; ⁊ mid swylce reafe he inn eode, mid swylce gange utt. Gif he wif silf hæbbe, gange heo ut mid him. Gyf se hlaford þonne him wif sealde, sy heo ⁊ hyre bearn þæs hlafordes. Gyf se þeowa þonne cwæþe: ‘nelle ic fram minum hlaforde ne fram minum wife ne fram minum bearne ne fram minum yrfe’, bringe hine þonne his hlaford to þære dura þæs temples ⁊ þurhþyrlie his eare mid ane æle, to tacne þæt he sy æfre siððan þeow.

Si emeris seruum Hebreum sex annis seruiet tibi, in septimo egredietur liber gratis: cum quali ueste intrauerit, cum tali exeat; si habens uxorem, et uxor egredietur simul. Sin autem dominus dederit illi uxorem, et peperit filios et filias, mulier et liberi eius erunt domini sui; ipse uero exibit cum uestitu suo. Quodsi dixerit seruus: ‘Diligo dominum meum et uxorem ac liberos, non egrediar liber’, offerat eum dominus diis, et applicabitur ad hostium et postes, perforabitque aurem eius subula; et erit ei seruus in ęternum.

Þis sint ða domas þe ðu him settan scealt: Gif hwa gebycgge cristenne þeow, VI gear ðeowige he; ðy siofoðan beo he frioh órceapunga; mid swelce hrægle he ineode, mid swelce gange he ut. Gif he wif self hæbbe, gange hio ut mid him. Gif se hlaford him þonne wif sealde, sie hio ⁊ hire bearn þæs hlafordes. Gif se þeowa þonne cweðe: "Nelle ic from minum hlaforde ne from minum wife, ne from minum bearne ne from minum ierfe," brenge hine þonne his hlaford to ðære dura þæs temples ⁊ þurhþyrlige his eare mid æle, to tácne þæt he sie æfre siððan þeow.

Dies sind die Gebote, die du ihnen setzen sollst: Wenn jemand einen christlichen Sklaven kauft, diene dieser als Sklav 6 Jahre; im siebenten sei er frei ohne Lösegeld; mit welchem Gewande er hineinkam, mit solchem trete er aus; wenn er selbst eine Ehefrau hat, trete sie mit ihm aus. Wenn dagegen der Herr ihm eine Frau gegeben hat, so sei sie und ihre Nachkommenschaft des Herrn [eigen]. Wenn jedoch der Sklav spricht: ‘Ich will nicht fort von meinem Herrn, noch von meinem Weibe, noch von meiner Nachkommenschaft, noch von meiner Habe’, so bringe ihn dann sein Herr zu der Thür des Tempels und durchbohre sein [des Sklaven] Ohr mit einer Ahle, zum Zeichen, dass dieser immer hinfort Sklav sei.

These are the commandments that you shall set for them: If someone buys a Christian slave, let him serve as a slave 6 years; in the seventh let him be free without ransom; with whatever garment he came in, with such let him go out; if he himself has a wife, let her go out with him. If, however, the master has given him a wife, then let her and her offspring be the master’s [own]. But if the slave says: ‘I will not go away from my master, nor from my wife, nor from my offspring, nor from my property’, then let his master bring him to the door of the temple and pierce his [the slave’s] ear with an awl, as a sign that he is to be a slave for ever after.

These are the judgments you shall set before them: If someone purchases a Christian slave, let him serve for six years; on the seventh, let him go free without payment; with such clothing as he entered, let him depart with such. If he has a wife, let her go out with him. But if it was the lord who gave him his wife, let her and her children be the lord’s. If, however, the slave should say: “I will not [depart] from my lord nor from my wife nor from my child nor from my possessions,” then his lord shall bring him to the door of the temple and pierce through his ear with an awl, as a token that he shall be thenceforth and forever a slave.

Das Gebot wollte durch Verchristlichung (s. o. Einl. 31) vielleicht zu Freilassungen (s. d. Gl 2), besonders der aus Not Selbstverknechteten (Earle Landcha. 275), anregen. Es ward nie praktisch, auch nicht auf Königs- oder Klostergütern. ‘Christlich’ steht wohl nicht im Ggs. zu ‘heidnischem Sklaven’, der damals nur ein kriegsgefangener Nordmann sein konnte, vom Agsächs. Herrn gewiss schnell zur Taufe gezwungen, sondern gibt nur Nachdruck

By Christianizing it (see above Introduction 31) the commandment was perhaps meant to encourage manumissions (see that word in Gl 2), especially of those who had enslaved themselves out of need (Earle Landcha. 275). It never became practice, not even on royal or monastic estates. ‘Christian’ is probably not in contrast to a ‘heathen slave’, who at that time could only have been a Northman taken prisoner in war, certainly soon forced into baptism by his A.-S. lord, but merely adds emphasis
H verstand das im 11. Jh. veraltete Wort nicht mehr; sein Ersatz bed. sinnlos ‘im Kaufgeschäft’
H no longer understood the word, which was obsolete in the 11th cent.; his substitute means, senselessly, ‘in the business of buying’

Im Agsä. Recht ward eine Freie nicht etwa (wie aus dem hieraus Umgekehrten scheinen könnte) durch Verknechtung des Mannes unfrei; vgl. Gl Ehe 5
In A.-S. law a free woman did not, say, become unfree through the enslavement of her husband (as might appear from the converse of this); cf. Gl Ehe 5
‘child’ earlier scholars; but see the Vulgate

Ælfred scheint an die Parallelstelle Deut. 15, 16 zu denken: wenn der Sklav diligat domum tuam et bene sibi apud te esse sentiat, vielleicht nahm er domus als Domäne des Herrschaftsguts; denn der Sklav ist ihm ein angesiedelter Knecht, laut eigenen Besitzes, worunter zunächst Vieh zu denken ist. In solchem Falle richtet sich das Gebot gegen Austreibung der niedersten Gutsabhängigen

Ælfred seems to be thinking of the parallel passage Deut. 15, 16: if the slave diligat domum tuam et bene sibi apud te esse sentiat, he perhaps took domus as the demesne of the manor; for to him the slave is a settled serf, as shown by his own property, by which cattle are to be understood in the first place. In that case the commandment is directed against the eviction of the lowest dependants of the estate

Auch Ælfric übersetzt þæs haligdomes dura (obwohl die Parallele Deut. 15, 17 ianua domus tuae deutlich dagegen spricht), vielleicht aus missverstandenem afferat diis (‘Richtern’, für die Af unten El 37 ‘Gott’ falsch einsetzt), was er wie Ælfred fortlässt. Vgl. zu dieser Verkirchlichung Gl Freilassung 1b. Sklavenkauf an der Kirchtür kannten die Agsa.; Kemble Saxons I 501. 508

Ælfric too translates þæs haligdomes dura (although the parallel Deut. 15, 17 ianua domus tuae clearly tells against it), perhaps from a misunderstood afferat diis (‘judges’, for which Af below, El 37, wrongly substitutes ‘God’), which he, like Ælfred, omits. On this ecclesiasticizing cf. Gl Freilassung 1b. The Anglo-Saxons knew the purchase of slaves at the church door; Kemble Saxons I 501. 508
